name: MonarchPriorityPicker
title: PriorityPicker
wrapsNative: MonarchButton (androidx.compose.material3.Button) or androidx.compose.material3.IconButton with androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu and DropdownMenuItem; androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas for the level shapes
summary: A menu button that shows and changes how urgent an issue is, on the urgent, high, medium, low and no-priority scale, where every level has its own shape and name.
whenToUse: For the priority of an issue, a ticket or a task in a form, a detail panel or a list row; use MonarchPriorityGlyph alone where the priority is shown but not changed.
whenNotToUse: For a scale the product defines itself use MonarchRolePicker or a Material 3 ExposedDropdownMenuBox. For a status use MonarchStatusBadge.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPriorityPicker(value: MonarchPriorityLevel?, onValueChange: (MonarchPriorityLevel) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchPriorityPickerSize = MonarchPriorityPickerSize.Md, levels: List<MonarchPriorityLevel> = MonarchPriorityLevel.entries, showLabel: Boolean = true, enabled: Boolean = true, trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchPriorityPickerLabels = MonarchPriorityPickerLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, initiallyOpen: Boolean = false)
@Composable fun MonarchPriorityGlyph(level: MonarchPriorityLevel, modifier: Modifier = Modifier)
enum class MonarchPriorityLevel(val number: Int) { Urgent, High, Medium, Low, None; companion object { fun fromNumber(number: Int?): MonarchPriorityLevel } }
class MonarchPriorityPickerLabels(trigger: ((String) -> String)? = null, urgent: String? = null, high: String? = null, medium: String? = null, low: String? = null, none: String? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The current level; null shows No priority.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the level the person chooses. Choosing the current level only closes the menu.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm for a dense row, Md for a form. The touch target is 48dp at both sizes.

options.name: levels
options.description: The levels offered, in menu order.

options.name: showLabel
options.description: Shows the level's name next to its shape. false gives a shape-only icon button, still named.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the menu can be opened.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: A decorative icon after the name, such as a down chevron. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Priority: %s" and the five level names.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the trigger's press and focus interactions.

options.name: level
options.description: MonarchPriorityGlyph: the level whose shape is drawn, 14dp by default.

states.name: levels
states.description: Urgent: a filled tile with an exclamation mark in the strong danger color. High, medium, low: three, two or one filled bars of three (high in the strong warning color). No priority: three dashes in the muted color.

states.name: menu open
states.description: A Material 3 dropdown menu with each level's shape and name; the current level is selected and has a radio button.

states.name: shape only
states.description: An icon button with the shape; the name stays in what TalkBack reads.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The button's disabled colors; the menu does not open.

appearance: The trigger is a secondary MonarchButton with the level's shape and name. Shapes use the strong danger color for urgent, the strong warning color for high, the default text color for medium and low and the muted text color for no priority; bars that are not filled are outlined in the strong border color. High contrast themes use their stronger roles.
platformNotes: The web draws the empty bars as the mark color at 45% opacity; Monarch never dims with alpha, so they are outlined in the strong border color. The web's priorityFromNumber and priorityToNumber are MonarchPriorityLevel.fromNumber and number. The web's PriorityGlyph is MonarchPriorityGlyph. The shapes are drawn on a Canvas from the web's 14-unit grid; they are part of the component, not an icon set. iOS documents this entry as the system menu Picker with SF Symbols and ships no type; Android builds it, because a Material 3 menu takes any composable as an item's icon, so the web's shapes can be kept.
accessibility: The trigger has the drop-down list role and is read as "Priority: High".
In the menu each level is read by name; the current one has the selected state and a radio button.
The shapes are hidden from TalkBack; each level has its own shape and name, so the priority never depends on color alone.
The trigger has a touch target of at least 48dp at both sizes, with or without the name.
The name scales with the font size setting without being cut.
edgeCases: value null and MonarchPriorityLevel.None look and read the same.
Offer a subset of levels with levels; the current level is still shown on the trigger even when it is not offered.
fromNumber maps any number other than 0 to 4 to None.
The bars do not mirror right to left, as on the web: they rise from start to end in every direction.

examples.title: Priority picker
examples.template:
MonarchPriorityPicker(
    value = priority,
    onValueChange = { priority = it },
    initiallyOpen = true,
    trailingIcon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.ChevronDown, contentDescription = null) },
)
